newsitem.title: BELGIUM: PetroFina aims for profit rise to yr 2000.
newsitem.headline: PetroFina aims for profit rise to yr 2000.

text.p: Earnings at Belgian oil and gas group PetroFina nearly doubled in the first four months of 1997, putting it on track for a higher full-year result, chief executive officer Francois Cornelis said on Monday.

"1997 will be another important year. Our annual budget foresees new improvement in the group's result and there is no reason this should not happen," Cornelis told the company's annual shareholders meeting. "At the end of April, the group's result was estimated to be seven billion Belgian francs, compared with 3.9 billion in 1996. Second quarter trends are favourable, in spite of the crude price drop to $18."

PetroFina group net earnings in 1996 rose to 16.05 billion Belgian francs from 11.61 billion in 1995 as a firm upstream performance was complemented in the second half by better refining and chemicals margins.
PetroFina group net profit in the first half of 1996 amounted to 6.70 billion francs, barely changed from 6.62 billion in 1995.

Cornelis said that despite the drop in crude oil prices the group was still benefiting from a higher dollar (about 35 francs vs about 32 francs at end of 1996), sustained demand for chemicals and higher refining margins and demand for American gasoline.
"We are entering what is known as the American driving season...We are enjoying the moment, but we cannot say how long the margins will be there," Cornelis told a news conference held before the AGM.

He noted, however, the group's key Antwerp refinery, which in 1996 accounted for around half daily refining capacity of 650,000 barrels, was still benefitting from a big price differential between light and heavier crudes, which it has been specially adapted to handle.
For eighteen months until mid-1996 the differential was around $50. "Now it's between $90 to $100," Cornelis said.
Cornelis said the group had also set itself the objective of returning to pre-1992 levels of profitability by the year 2000.
"Over the next three years, the group's ambition is to double the average results obtained by PetroFina from 1992 to 1996," Cornelis told the AGM.

Based on reported group net results for the period, this would place the target profit at over 19.9 billion Belgian francs, a level not seen since 1990, when it paid a gross dividend of 560 francs. 1996's dividend was 400 francs.
"We are working to drive cash flow to 50 billion francs a year...when we could reinvest 35 billion francs in the business and still pay a full dividend as we used to before 1992," Cornelis said.

"To fully cover the (560 franc) dividend we have to get back to a 20 billion franc net result, which is the plan for 2000. This would give us a return on equity of 15 percent. In 1996 it was 13 percent," he added.
Cornelis said PetroFina's investment budget for 1997 was 37 billion Belgian francs, up from 34 billion in 1996.
